note: All statuses, severities and confidence values below are Claude's preliminary drafts. Nothing here is a confirmed vulnerability or final severity. No dynamic request was executed to reproduce any case; expected results are derived purely from static tracing of app/main.py and app/policy.py.

authentication.description: Read 'authorization' header; require exactly 2 whitespace-separated parts with case-insensitive scheme 'bearer'; else deny(401, missing_or_malformed_credential).
SHA-256 hash the bearer token and look up app/seed.py:44 unique 'token_hash' column via parameterized query.
Matching row becomes request.state.identity and the 'actor' used by every downstream authorization decision; no header/query/body value other than Authorization participates.

authorization_me.description: Depends(authenticate) only; returns public(actor) i.e. the caller's own row. No object/tenant check needed because target==actor by construction.

authorization_list.description: Role-only gate: role!='admin' -> (False,'admin_required'); else (True,'tenant_administrator'). No tenant check performed here.
deny(403,reason) if not permitted, else allow(reason).
Tenant scoping for the returned list is enforced ONLY by the SQL predicate 'WHERE tenant_id = ?' bound to actor['tenant_id'], outside of policy.py.

authorization_detail.description: Depends(authenticate); target row fetched by 'user_id' alone with NO tenant predicate -- existence is resolved before any authorization check.
No row for that user_id anywhere in the database -> deny(404, unknown_user).
request.state.target_user_id set for audit only; policy.authorize_detail(actor, target) invoked.
actor.tenant_id != target.tenant_id -> (False,'tenant_boundary'). Applies uniformly, including to admin actors -- prevents cross-tenant admin escalation.
Else (same tenant, not self, not admin) -> (False,'owner_required').
deny(403,reason) if not permitted, else allow(reason); return public(target).

supporting_controls.description: public() projects exactly FIELDS=(user_id,tenant_id,role,name,email,phone), matching security-requirements.json approved_public_fields; token_hash is never included.
deny() always raises HTTPException with a generic reason string ('Unauthorized'/'Not found'/'Forbidden'); protected fields are never placed in the body.

Audit middleware logs request_id, run_id, route, method, status, response size, elapsed_ms, source_ip, identity alias, tenant_id, target_user_id, decision, reason -- comment at line 64 states raw URLs/headers/tokens/bodies are never logged; confirmed by code, no such fields are referenced.

correlation_id(): client-supplied X-Request-ID/X-Run-ID are honored only if they parse as a UUID, else a fresh uuid4 is generated server-side; these values are never used in any authorization decision.
docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url disabled, reducing schema-based information disclosure.

findings.title: Cross-tenant object-existence oracle via differentiated 404/403 on GET /api/users/{user_id}
findings.trust_boundary_ref: assessment-brief.en.md #5 item 3: 'finding an object does not mean the actor is authorized to read it'

evidence.detail: query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE user_id = ?', (user_id,)) has no tenant predicate; runs before any authorization decision.
if not rows: deny(request,404,'unknown_user') -- executes prior to policy.authorize_detail.
policy.authorize_detail() runs only after existence is already established; a cross-tenant existing target yields 403 tenant_boundary, distinct from the 404 for a non-existent id.
tenant_boundary reason is only reachable once a row was found -- so 403 tenant_boundary is itself proof that the id exists somewhere in the whole database, not just the caller's tenant.

findings.impact_draft: Any authenticated actor, including the lowest-privileged 'user' role that has no list access, can determine whether a given user_id exists anywhere in the system (any tenant) by observing 404 vs 403, without ever being authorized to view that record. This does not by itself expose protected fields (name/email/phone), so it does not meet the brief's 'confirmed_violation' bar on its own, but it weakens tenant-boundary secrecy and is a building block for targeted probing if user_id values become guessable (see Observation O1).
findings.root_cause_draft: Existence resolution (app/main.py:112-114) is performed before, and independently of, the authorization decision (app/main.py:117 / app/policy.py:10-15), and the two negative outcomes are surfaced with distinguishable status codes/reasons.
findings.remediation_direction_draft: Resolve the target using a tenant-scoped query for non-admin-cross-tenant checks, or normalize the two deny outcomes (unauthorized cross-tenant reference and truly unknown id) to the same status/response shape, consistent with a deny-by-default 'do not confirm existence to unauthorized callers' pattern. Final approach is Codex's/Security Engineer's call.

findings.title: List-endpoint tenant scoping is implemented outside the centralized authorization policy module

evidence.detail: authorize_list(actor) only checks actor['role'] == 'admin'; it never receives or checks tenant_id, and returns no scope/filter information.
Tenant filtering for the list response is implemented solely as the SQL predicate 'WHERE tenant_id = ?' bound to actor['tenant_id'], inline in the route handler rather than inside app/policy.py.

findings.impact_draft: Today, AUTHZ-LIST-02 is satisfied because main.py:108 always binds the actor's own tenant_id. However, the authorization module that centralizes every other allow/deny decision (authorize_list, authorize_detail) does not own this scope rule, so it is not covered by any policy-level unit test aimed at policy.py, and a future change to the route (added filter/pagination/export parameter, or a 'cross-tenant admin' feature) could silently drop tenant scoping without touching policy.py at all.
findings.root_cause_draft: Separation-of-duties gap: 'is this action allowed' (policy.py) and 'what object scope is allowed' (main.py inline SQL) are split across two layers with no shared enforcement point or test surface.
findings.remediation_direction_draft: Move tenant scoping into the policy layer, e.g. have policy expose a scope/filter (such as a required tenant_id predicate or a small scope_list(actor) helper) that main.py must consume, so the rule is unit-testable alongside authorize_detail's tenant_boundary check. Final approach is Codex's/Security Engineer's call.

observations_out_of_primary_scope.title: Fixture user_id values are generated from a fixed-seed PRNG, separate from the CSPRNG used for bearer tokens

evidence.detail: create_fixture(seed: int = 42): rng = random.Random(seed) -- deterministic, non-cryptographic PRNG with a fixed default seed.
user_id built from rng.getrandbits(128) formatted as a UUID; reproducible for anyone who knows the seed.
By contrast, bearer tokens use secrets.token_urlsafe(32), a CSPRNG -- correctly treated as the actual secret.

observations_out_of_primary_scope.reason_recorded_as_observation_not_findi: assessment-brief.en.md section 6 explicitly places 'user ID enumeration' out of scope, and this is fixture/test-data generation code, not the reviewed application's authorization decision path; user_id is never trusted as a credential anywhere in app/policy.py or app/main.py.
observations_out_of_primary_scope.relevance: If combined with F1, predictable user_id generation would make the existence oracle more practically exploitable in a non-test deployment; recommend flagging to the fixture/tooling owner rather than treating as an app-code defect.

observations_out_of_primary_scope.title: Token-hash lookup uses non-constant-time string equality at the database layer

evidence.detail: hashlib.sha256(...).hexdigest() compared via SQL 'WHERE token_hash = ?'; SQLite string equality is not guaranteed constant-time.

observations_out_of_primary_scope.assessment: Practical timing exploitation over a network is regarded as very low feasibility (I/O jitter dominates; a digest, not the raw secret, is being compared). Recorded for completeness/defense-in-depth only.

no_violation_observed.basis: app/main.py:81-89; single unique token_hash column (app/seed.py:44) maps to exactly one actor; generic 401 on missing/malformed/unknown credential.
No route in app/main.py reads any client header/query/body value to derive tenant_id/role/user_id; actor is always the DB row bound to the validated token.
app/main.py:97-100 returns public(actor) only, i.e. exactly the caller's own row.
app/policy.py:13-15: non-admin actor is allowed only when actor.user_id==target.user_id.
app/policy.py:11-12: tenant_boundary check applies unconditionally, including to admin actors, before the self/admin allow branch.
app/policy.py:4-6: only role=='admin' is permitted to call GET /api/users.
app/main.py:108: query is always scoped to actor['tenant_id'] as currently written (see F2 for a structural caveat, not a present violation).
app/main.py:94-95 public() whitelist matches approved_public_fields exactly; token_hash and other DB columns are never serialized.
app/main.py:76-79 deny() always returns a fixed generic string per status; no code path places name/email/phone or credentials into an error body.

app/main.py:64-74 log line fields are limited to ids/route/method/status/size/timing/alias/tenant_id/target_user_id/decision/reason; no Authorization header, token, or full profile field is referenced anywhere in the logging code.
